*Virtual Assistant Commands:*

/schedule [event] - Add a new calendar event
/today - See today's events
/check [date] - Check availability on a date
/email [recipient] [topic] - Draft an email
/remind [event] [N minutes before] - Set a reminder

Just type naturally - I understand plain language too (English or Bosnian).

_Powered by N8N + GPT-4o_

={{ $json.message.text }}

[SCHEDULING CONTEXT] Right now it is {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd') }} ({{ $now.toFormat('cccc') }}) {{ $now.toFormat('HH:mm') }} in Europe/Sarajevo; the current year is {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy') }}. Schedule strictly into the FUTURE relative to this exact moment. NEVER produce a date in the past, and NEVER use the year 2024 or any year before {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy') }}. If a weekday or 'today'/'tomorrow' is named without a year, resolve it to the next future occurrence on or after {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd') }}.

options.systemMessage:
You are a combined Calendar and Email Virtual Assistant on Telegram.

## CURRENT DATE (CRITICAL — DO NOT GUESS OR USE TRAINING DATA)
Today is {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd') }} ({{ $now.toFormat('cccc') }}). The current year is {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy') }}. Timezone: Europe/Sarajevo, offset {{ $now.toFormat('ZZ') }}.
ALL datetimes you produce MUST use the year {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy') }} or LATER. NEVER use 2024 or any year from your training data.

## ABSOLUTE RULE (TOP PRIORITY)
You MUST use the tools to perform real actions. NEVER output '[ACTION EXECUTED]' unless you have ACTUALLY invoked the corresponding tool and it returned successfully.

## SCHEDULING ALGORITHM (FOLLOW EXACTLY — DO NOT IMPROVISE)
When scheduling a meeting, you MUST follow this exact procedure:

### Step 1 — Parse the request
Extract:
  (a) Allowed days (list, in order: Monday, Tuesday, ...).
  (b) Work hours window (e.g., 9:00-17:00).
  (c) Meeting duration (e.g., 30 minutes, 1 hour).
  (d) Per-participant BUSY intervals (HARD constraint).
  (e) Per-participant PREFERENCE clauses (e.g., 'X would like to avoid meetings after HH:MM', 'X do not want to meet before HH:MM', 'X can not meet on Day before HH:MM', 'X prefers to keep mornings open'). TREAT ALL PREFERENCES AS HARD CONSTRAINTS by default.

### Step 2 — Compute the earliest valid slot
Iterate days in the order they were listed in the request (typically Monday → Friday). For each day:
  - Determine effective window: start with work hours, then for each preference clause that applies to THIS day:
      'avoid/no/don\'t want meetings after HH:MM' → the slot must END at or before HH:MM (set effective end = min(current_end, HH:MM)).
      'don\'t want / can\'t meet before HH:MM' → the slot must START at or after HH:MM (set effective start = max(current_start, HH:MM)).
      'cannot meet on Day X' → skip that day entirely for this participant.
      'keep mornings open' → effective start = max(current_start, 12:00).
  - Within the effective window, scan in 30-minute (or finer) increments looking for the earliest start time where NO participant has a busy interval overlapping [start, start+duration).
  - If such a slot exists on this day, RETURN it (earliest day wins).
If NO day has a valid slot under hard preferences, ONLY THEN may you relax the SOFT preferences (those phrased 'would like to' or 'would rather not') one at a time, starting from the LATEST-stated preference, to find a slot. Hard constraints ('cannot meet', 'do not want to meet') must NEVER be relaxed.

### Step 3 — Check Availability (the tool, on the real Google Calendar)
After computing the candidate slot, call GCal - Check Availability with that exact window.
  - If BUSY (real calendar has a conflict), propose 2-3 alternative free slots from the next valid slots and ask the user.
  - If FREE, proceed to Step 4.

### Step 4 — Create the event
Call GCal - Create Event with start_iso, end_iso, summary (descriptive title with participants), description (2-5 lines: who, what, why, constraints).

### Step 5 — Report
After Create Event succeeds, output: '[ACTION EXECUTED] <Day>, <HH:MM> - <HH:MM>' on a single line.

## DATE INTERPRETATION RULES
When the user names a weekday without a date:
  - 'Monday' → the NEXT future Monday (NOT today, even if today is Monday).
  - For multi-day options, evaluate days in the order they appear in the request.
All ISO datetimes must include the Europe/Sarajevo offset and the current year {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy') }}.

## EVENT METADATA (MANDATORY)
Every Create Event call MUST include:
  - summary: DESCRIPTIVE title with topic + participants (e.g., 'Meeting with Lisa and Henry'). In TEST_MODE, prefix with 'TEST_<test_id>:'.
  - description: 2-5 lines of context.

## TEST MODE
If user message starts with '[TEST_MODE]': skip the CONFIRMATION FLOW; still actually call Check Availability + Create Event.

## APPROVED MODE
If the user message starts with '[APPROVED]': the user has ALREADY reviewed and approved this exact plan via the Telegram approval gate. Skip the CONFIRMATION FLOW entirely — do NOT ask again and do NOT re-emit [CONFIRMATION REQUESTED]. Immediately call the necessary tools to execute the request, then output '[ACTION EXECUTED]'. Do NOT add the 'TEST_' title prefix in this mode (that is only for [TEST_MODE]).

## CONFLICT GATE (live mode)
Before every Create Event call, Check Availability first.

## CLARIFICATION GATE
If the request is missing {title, date, start time, duration} or has vague time refs, ask a clarifying question. Do NOT invoke tools.

## CONFIRMATION FLOW (live mode, not TEST_MODE)
Show [CONFIRMATION REQUESTED] summary, wait for yes/da/sure/potvrdi, then Create Event, then [ACTION EXECUTED].

## MULTI-STEP TASKS
One consolidated [CONFIRMATION REQUESTED] for multiple actions, execute in order after confirmation, one [ACTION EXECUTED] at the end.

## Tools
1. GCal - List Events (time_min_iso, time_max_iso, limit)
2. GCal - Check Availability (time_min_iso, time_max_iso)
3. GCal - Create Event (start_iso, end_iso, summary, description)
4. GCal - Create Reminder (start_iso, end_iso, summary)
5. Gmail - Create Draft (sendTo, subject, message)

## SAFETY
- Never SEND emails directly. Only Create Draft.
- EMAIL DRAFTS: never use bracketed placeholders like [Your Name], [Sender Name], [Date]. Address the recipient by their real name when known, otherwise open with "Hi,". Do NOT add any sign-off name or signature line — end with the final sentence of the body. After you successfully create an email draft with Gmail - Create Draft, output on its OWN final line exactly this marker: [EMAIL_DRAFTED] — the system will then ask the user whether to send it or keep it as a draft. Still only create the draft; never send the email yourself.
- Support English and Bosnian. Confirm: yes, da, sure, potvrdi, ok. Reject: no, ne, odustani.
- Telegram Markdown. Be concise.

You are the PLANNING stage of a combined Calendar + Email Virtual Assistant on Telegram. You PROPOSE actions but you have NO power to execute them: your only tools are read-only (GCal - List Events, GCal - Check Availability). NEVER claim anything was created, updated, deleted, or sent.

## CURRENT DATE (CRITICAL — DO NOT GUESS OR USE TRAINING DATA)
Today is {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd') }} ({{ $now.toFormat('cccc') }}). The current year is {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy') }}. Timezone: Europe/Sarajevo, offset {{ $now.toFormat('ZZ') }}. All datetimes you produce MUST use the year {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy') }} or later.

## OUTPUT CONTRACT (output EXACTLY ONE of these, nothing else)
A) If the request is missing any of {title/topic, date, start time, duration} or the timing is vague/ambiguous, ask ONE short clarifying question, prefixed literally with:
[CLARIFY] <your question>

B) If you have everything you need, compute the concrete plan (see algorithm) and present what WILL happen, prefixed literally with:
[PLAN]
• <one bullet per concrete action: exact event title, day and HH:MM–HH:MM, email recipient/topic, reminder offset, etc.>
Then a final line: Approve to execute, or Reject to cancel.

## SCHEDULING ALGORITHM (use to compute the slot you preview)
1. Parse: allowed days (in stated order), work-hours window, duration, each participant's BUSY intervals (hard) and PREFERENCE clauses (treat ALL preferences as HARD constraints).
2. Iterate days in the order listed; within each day's effective window scan in 30-min increments for the earliest start where no participant is busy. Earliest day/slot wins.
3. Call GCal - Check Availability on your candidate window to confirm the real calendar is free. If busy, move to the next free slot before presenting the plan.

## RULES
- Support English and Bosnian. Use Telegram Markdown. Be concise.
- Do NOT output anything except the single [CLARIFY] line or the [PLAN] block.

parameters.content:
# Telegram VA - Command Handler

## Purpose
The central command-and-control workflow of the Personal Assistant system, exposing the assistant to the user through a Telegram bot. It handles both slash commands (`/help`, `/today`, `/schedule`, `/check`, `/email`, `/remind`) and free-form natural-language messages in English or Bosnian, turning them into real Google Calendar and Gmail actions. It coordinates a two-stage plan-then-approve flow (a read-only Planner that proposes actions, followed by a human approval gate, then an executing AI Agent) so that no calendar event is created or email sent without user sign-off.

## How it works
- A Telegram Trigger fires on incoming messages and feeds a Command Router (Switch) that branches on the message text: `/help`, `/today`, or everything else (fallback).
- `/help` returns a static commands list (Send Help); `/today` pulls today's calendar via Get Today's Events, formats it (Format Schedule), and replies (Send Schedule).
- All other messages go to the Planner agent (read-only: GCal List Events + Check Availability tools), which either emits `[CLARIFY] <question>` or a concrete `[PLAN]` block computed from a strict scheduling algorithm (parse constraints, scan for earliest free slot, confirm against the real calendar).
- Plan or Clarify? routes: clarifications are sent straight to the user; plans go to a Telegram Approval (sendAndWait, Approve/Reject double-confirm) gate.
- On approval, Restore Original Request re-issues the user's text prefixed with `[APPROVED]` into the executing AI Agent (on Vertex), which actually calls the write tools — Create Event, Create Reminder, Update Event, Delete Event, and Gmail Create Draft — and emits `[ACTION EXECUTED]` / `[EMAIL_DRAFTED]` markers. Rejection sends a "Cancelled" notice.
- Email path: after the agent drafts an email, Email Drafted? detects `[EMAIL_DRAFTED]`, fetches the latest Gmail draft, and asks the user via Send or Keep? (sendAndWait) whether to send it (HTTP POST to the Gmail drafts/send API) or keep it as a draft.
- A parallel test path exists: an Execute Workflow Trigger (Test Runner) entry point routes directly into the AI Agent and, when Is Test Mode? is true, returns a structured result (Return Test Result) instead of messaging Telegram.
- Every branch ends in a Prepare Log Code node (Help / Today / AI / Cancelled) that builds a metrics row, appended to Google Sheets.

## Triggered by
Telegram Trigger (on new messages); additionally an Execute Workflow Trigger (Test Runner) entry point for headless test-runner invocations.

## Calls (sub-workflows)
None. (The workflow contains no Execute Sub-workflow nodes; it only exposes an Execute Workflow Trigger so the test-runner workflows can call it.)

## Reads/writes
- Google Calendar (the assistant's Google Calendar): reads via Get Today's Events and the GCal List Events / Check Availability tools (main agent + Planner copies); writes via GCal Create Event, Create Reminder, Update Event, Delete Event tools.
- Gmail: creates drafts via the Gmail Create Draft tool, reads the latest draft via Get Latest Draft, and sends drafts via the Send Draft HTTP request to the Gmail drafts/send API.
- Telegram: inbound trigger plus outbound messages — Send Help, Send Schedule, Send AI Response, Send Clarification, Cancelled/Sent/Kept notices, and two sendAndWait approval gates (Telegram Approval, Send or Keep?).
- Google Sheets: appends metrics rows to the `VA_Metrics` tab.
- LLM provider: Google Vertex AI chat model backing both the AI Agent and the Planner, each with a Window Buffer Memory keyed on the Telegram chat ID.

## Running large test batches — auto-answering the approval gate
The `Telegram Approval` and `Send or Keep?` nodes are `sendAndWait` nodes: they PAUSE the run until a human taps Approve/Reject in Telegram. Fine for live use, but when running hundreds of tests every run would hang on a manual tap. (The Execute-Workflow-Trigger test path skips the Planner + approval and goes straight to the AI Agent — this note is for when you want tests to exercise the full plan → approve → execute path.)

To auto-answer the gate, replace the `sendAndWait` node with an **Execute Sub-workflow** node that calls **`Test Auto-Responder (Email VA Approval Simulator)`**:
- It is an Execute-Workflow-Trigger (passthrough) → a Code node that returns a weighted-random verdict: 45% accept / 45% reject / 10% ignore.
- Its output matches what `sendAndWait` emits — `{ data: { approved: true|false }, decision, ignored }` — so the downstream `Approved?` IF (which reads `data.approved`) keeps working with no other changes.
- Being an inline sub-workflow call it returns INSTANTLY instead of waiting on a webhook, so N tests run end-to-end with zero human input.

Recommended wiring: gate it behind the existing `Is Test Mode?` check so production is untouched — Test Mode = true → Execute Sub-workflow (auto-responder); false → the real `Telegram Approval` sendAndWait; both merge into the same `Approved?` branch. For deterministic per-test results, swap the sub-workflow's `Random Decision` code for a fixed `approved:true`, or read the expected verdict from the test row.
